title: Om Prakash v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Tarun Agarwala, J.; Shri Narayan Shukla, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; relegated to CGRF and Ombudsman under clause 7.10.
headnote: After a permanent disconnection was allowed, a demand for electricity arrears and a recovery citation followed. The Division Bench held that the consumer’s remedy lay before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and the Ombudsman under clause 7.10 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and dismissed the writ on the ground of alternative remedy.
facts: The petitioner, Om Prakash, applied to the distribution licensee for a permanent disconnection of his electricity supply. That application was allowed. Thereafter a demand for arrears of electricity dues was raised against him. He did not pay those arrears, and a recovery citation was consequently issued. He then invoked the writ jurisdiction of the Allahabad High Court, seeking to challenge the demand and the recovery proceedings initiated against him.

holding_units.holding: A consumer faced with a demand for electricity arrears and a recovery citation after a permanent disconnection has a statutory remedy before the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum and the Ombudsman under clause 7.10 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ petition was dismissed on that ground of alternative remedy.

not_decided.point: Validity of the arrears demand and the recovery citation
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the merits of the demand or the recovery citation, relegating the petitioner to the clause 7.10 forum.
